channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dissolves Parliament, Calls for Early Elections
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has signed a decree to prematurely terminate the powers of all levels of parliament. The Central Election Commission is tasked with organizing and holding early parliamentary elections. The government and local executive bodies are instructed to provide organizational, logistical, and financial support for the upcoming vote.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Financial Expert Compares Pension Annuities, UIP, and Unified Pension Fund Options
item.description: A financial expert in Kazakhstan has analyzed the benefits of pension annuities, individual voluntary pension (UIP), and the Unified Pension Fund (ENPF). She advises a balanced approach considering age, savings, retirement plans, and risk tolerance. Annuities protect against outliving savings, while UIP offers potential investment growth.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Japarov Discusses Divorce and Family Obligations in Botken
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov addressed issues of divorce and family responsibilities during a visit to Botken. A woman sought his assistance, reporting a legal dispute with her husband over property division. The president's remarks highlighted societal challenges related to marital obligations and their dissolution.

item.title: OIC Delegation Meets Taliban in Kabul, Omits Women's Rights from Statement
item.description: An Organization of Islamic Cooperation delegation met with senior Taliban officials in Kabul to discuss the country's situation. However, the OIC's public statement following the visit failed to mention the Taliban's restrictions on women and girls' rights, including education and employment bans.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Ministry Condemns Attacks on Saudi Arabia as 'Regrettable'
item.description: The Taliban's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has called recent attacks on Saudi Arabian airports 'regrettable,' condemning any actions threatening civilian lives and safety. The ministry urged all parties to exercise restraint and avoid escalating the situation, emphasizing the need for de-escalation and civilian security.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Collecting Tax Debts from Individuals
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance has approved updated forms for tax authorities to collect overdue taxes from individuals. These changes, effective October 19, 2026, include revised notices for tax debt payment and collection orders. The procedure for appealing these documents has also been clarified, allowing citizens three months to file a complaint with a higher tax authority.

item.title: Hidden Camera Captures Bribery 'Conveyor Belt' at Kyrgyzstan Border
item.description: A hidden camera has recorded what appears to be a systemic bribery operation at the border of Kyrgyzstan. The footage reveals a continuous flow of illicit payments, suggesting a widespread corruption issue. Authorities are expected to investigate the findings captured by the covert camera.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Advises Against Drinking Scalding Hot Tea and Coffee
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health warns that consuming excessively hot tea and coffee increases the risk of esophageal cancer. Citing a study, the ministry noted that drinking more than six cups of very hot beverages daily is linked to a 71% higher risk. They recommend letting drinks cool slightly to avoid damaging the esophageal lining.

item.title: Almaty Police Deny Rumors of Serial Killer Operating in the City
item.description: Almaty city police have refuted circulating messages about an unknown individual allegedly responsible for multiple murders in the city. The police department stated these claims are false and do not correspond to reality. They warned citizens about criminal liability for spreading obviously false information and urged reliance on official sources.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Needs-Based Criteria for State Benefits from 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan will implement new needs-based criteria for ten main state benefits, including child birth and disability payments, starting January 1, 2027. Individuals from affluent families may lose eligibility. The State Social Insurance Fund (SSIF) clarified that payments from the SSIF, funded by mandatory contributions, are separate from state benefits and available to insured workers.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Village Akims Election Marks Local Governance Reform
item.description: Direct elections for village akims in Kazakhstan are a key step in decentralizing state governance, according to expert Sabina Sadieva. Reforms began with increasing financial autonomy for villages and evolved to include direct public participation in forming local authorities. Around 2,500 village akims were elected directly by 2024.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Introduce QR Codes for Gasoline Origin Tracking
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to implement QR codes to track the origin of gasoline, from producer or importer to the gas station. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that technical and regulatory work is underway to ensure traceability of each fuel batch. This measure aims to improve gasoline quality control.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Emphasizes Criminal Liability for Polygamy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov stated that criminal cases should be initiated against men taking second or third wives. During a meeting in Batken, he urged men to be responsible towards their families. The president instructed the prosecutor's office and the Ministry of Internal Affairs to address this issue, as polygamy is punishable under Article 176 of the criminal code.

item.title: Belgian King and Queen Thank President Tokayev for Adjusting Schedule for Their Meeting
item.description: The King and Queen of Belgium expressed gratitude to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev for adjusting his schedule to meet with them. During their state visit to Astana, they praised Kazakhstan's development and noted the historical significance of their trip, which marks a new phase in bilateral partnership. They highlighted the strong relationship between Belgium and Kazakhstan, approaching 35 years of diplomatic ties.

item.title: Belgian King and Queen Explain Their Visit to Kazakhstan: 'A Very Important Country Showing High Development Rates'
item.description: The King and Queen of Belgium stated that Kazakhstan is a very important country for them, demonstrating high development rates, and expressed great interest in the entire Central Asian region. They believe their visit, accompanied by a representative delegation from various promising sectors, can elevate cooperation to a new level. They were deeply touched by President Tokayev's gesture of adjusting his schedule to accompany them.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Appoints Erkinjon Turdimov as Head of New Ministry of Education and Science
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the appointment of Erkinjon Turdimov as the head of the newly established Ministry of Education and Science. Speaking during a meeting in New Tashkent, Mirziyoyev emphasized the importance of education, stating he did not bring his most trusted personnel for education without reason. The new ministry aims to advance educational and scientific development in the country.

item.title: Scientists Warn of AI and Nuclear War Risks Threatening Humanity by 2100
item.description: Scientists from The Lancet commission studying global health threats warn that malicious AI use and nuclear conflict could endanger humanity within 75 years. Risks include AI-developed bioweapons and nuclear winter leading to mass starvation. While scenarios have high uncertainty, their potential scale necessitates political-level discussion.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Strengthen Regulation of Critical Digital Services After Yandex Outages
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to enhance regulation of critical digital services and ensure their integration with domestic infrastructure following extensive disruptions to Yandex. Minister of Digital Development, Innovations and Aerospace Industry, Zhaslan Madiev, stated that personal data of Kazakh citizens on Yandex is localized within the country, adhering to legal requirements. The government aims to mitigate future risks by mandating that such platforms connect to Kazakh infrastructure.

item.title: New Air Route Launched from Almaty to Hanoi and Prague
item.description: Vietjet Air has launched new flights from Almaty to Hanoi and Prague starting October 10th, operating twice weekly. The Airbus A330-300 aircraft will serve passengers on this route. Flight time from Almaty to Hanoi is approximately 6 hours and 10 minutes, and to Prague, 7 hours and 35 minutes. This route utilizes the 'fifth freedom of the air' rights, allowing carriage between Vietnam and the Czech Republic.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Economy Grows to $306 Billion; Almaty's Master Plan Revised; Maniac Scare Addressed
item.description: Kazakhstan's economy has expanded to $306 billion over seven years. In Almaty, revisions to the General Plan include preserving individual housing construction and abandoning road projections. Police have addressed public fears regarding reports of a 'maniac' in the city. Additionally, details emerge on how Baikonur navigated the 1990s.

item.title: Taliban Spokesperson Urges Pakistan to Address Internal Issues Instead of Making Accusations
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid responded to Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's remarks, urging Pakistani officials to focus on their "failed policies" rather than making accusations against the Taliban. Mujahid stated that such accusations are baseless and damage the negotiation process, highlighting Pakistan's political, security, social, and economic problems.

item.title: Three Department Heads Replaced in Abai Region, Kazakhstan
item.description: New heads have been appointed to three departments in Kazakhstan's Abai Region: water resources and irrigation, child rights protection, and tourism. The appointments include Askhat Ismailov for water resources, Ayzhan Mukatova for child rights, and Kuanysh Abildayev for tourism, according to the regional administration's press service.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Investment in New Tashkent with Entrepreneurs
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with entrepreneurs and investors in New Tashkent to discuss large-scale construction projects and the evolving business environment. A company director highlighted the rapid development of New Tashkent, attracting significant interest and trust from investors and the public. The company has invested nearly $60 million in its first project and plans further investments totaling $510 million.

item.title: Gasoline at Three Kazakhstan Gas Stations Fails to Meet Legal Requirements
item.description: Gasoline at three gas stations in Kazakhstan has been found to not meet legal requirements, according to Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov. Laboratory tests confirmed non-compliance in Almaty, Kyzylorda region, and Zhetysu region. Response measures have been taken in accordance with legislation. An interdepartmental commission is also investigating the production and sale of petroleum products following consumer complaints.

item.title: Uzbek President Appoints Former Governor Erkinjon Turdimov as New Minister of Education and Science
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev commented on the appointment of Erkinjon Turdimov as the new Minister of Education and Science, emphasizing a shift in focus towards quality over quantity. Mirziyoyev stated that bringing in an experienced former regional governor signifies a new approach to education, with a significantly increased focus from the state. Turdimov previously served as governor of several regions.

item.title: Chinese Company to Invest in New Gold Reserves Exploration in Kazakhstan
item.description: A Chinese company, Central Asia Kaisheng Minerals & Energy International Group Ltd., will invest at least 275 million tenge over six years to explore for new gold reserves in Kazakhstan. The Ministry of Industry and Construction confirmed the company holds exploration licenses. Further details on reserves will be determined by geological exploration results.

item.title: Afghan Spokesperson Accuses Pakistani Military of Undermining Bilateral Talks
item.description: Zabihullah Mujahid, spokesperson for Afghanistan's Islamic Emirate, accused Pakistani military circles of repeatedly sabotaging negotiations and efforts to resolve differences with Islamabad. He stated Afghanistan does not interfere in Pakistan's internal affairs and would not allow its territory to be used for insecurity. Mujahid claimed Pakistan's political leadership is willing to resolve issues, but military elements obstruct progress.

item.title: Almaty Interdepartmental Commission Resolves Issues for Esentai City and Monblanc Housing Projects
item.description: Almaty's interdepartmental commission has resolved issues for shareholders of several housing complexes, including Esentai City and Monblanc. Arrests on Esentai City property will be lifted, allowing construction to resume. An investor will continue Monblanc's construction and compensate shareholders. The commission is preparing agreements for the Monblanc project, which faced delays since 2016.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Holds Talks with King and Queen of Belgium
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held talks in a narrow format with the King and Queen of Belgium. Tokayev noted that the royal couple's first state visit to Kazakhstan marks a new stage in bilateral partnership. He emphasized Belgium as a reliable partner in Europe and highlighted the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year.

item.title: Kazakhstan Transported 77.8 Million Tons of Coal in First Nine Months
item.description: In the first nine months of the year, Kazakhstan's railway transport moved 77.8 million tons of coal, a 1.5% increase compared to the same period last year. Of this, 25 million tons were exported, and over 51 million tons were transported domestically. Preparations for the new heating season saw 28.1 million tons of coal transported between May 1 and September 30.

item.title: Turkmenistan Launches E-Visa System, But Service Remains Unavailable
item.description: Turkmenistan officially introduced an electronic visa system and canceled mandatory invitations on October 1. Online registration for visitors is also planned. However, nearly two weeks after the official launch, the services remain inaccessible. The e-visa portal evisa.migration.gov.tm is partially functional, allowing status checks and account logins, but visa applications and registrations are not yet possible.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Directs Mayors to Prepare Projects for New Tashkent Amidst Land Shortages
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev noted the lack of available land for new projects in existing Tashkent districts. He instructed district mayors to prepare project proposals for the New Tashkent area, with initial allocations of 100 hectares per district.

item.title: Uzbek President Emphasizes No Nationality for Capital, Ideas, or Labor
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that capital, advanced ideas, and honest labor have no nationality. He promoted the philosophy of "O‘z" for the country's economy, integrating concepts of Uzbekistan, change, self, and responsibility. This philosophy aims to foster an environment where investors are not distinguished as foreign or local.

item.title: Taliban Spokesman Responds to Pakistan's Security Allegations
item.description: Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid stated that blaming Afghanistan for Pakistan's problems will not resolve them. He accused Pakistani officials of baseless allegations and propaganda, urging constructive steps to address domestic issues. This follows Pakistan's Foreign Ministry claims of militant safe havens in Afghanistan, which the Taliban authorities deny.

item.title: Taliban Spokesperson Urges Pakistan to Respect Its People's Rights
item.description: Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid stated that Pakistan should not blame Afghanistan for its internal problems but rather respect its people's rights and opinions. Mujahid called Pakistan's accusations baseless and a sign of a failed policy, noting that internal challenges in Pakistan have negative regional consequences. He urged Pakistan to take constructive steps to resolve its domestic issues.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts Houthi Ballistic Missile Over Southwestern Region
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted a ballistic missile launched by Yemen's Houthi movement over Khamis Mushait in southwestern Saudi Arabia. The interception occurred shortly after Saudi Civil Defense issued a warning for the nearby city of Abha. This incident follows recent reports of Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh, which reportedly caused casualties.

item.title: New Tashkent Inaugurates $1 Billion in Projects, Launches $2.5 Billion More
item.description: In New Tashkent, projects worth $1 billion have been launched, with another $2.5 billion in projects initiated. The President participated in a ceremony to commission seven facilities and start the construction of ten major projects in the new city. This marks a significant development phase for the burgeoning urban area.

item.title: Shavkat Mirziyoyev Launches Construction of 10 Projects Worth $2.5 Billion in New Tashkent
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the ceremony to launch construction for 10 new projects in New Tashkent, with a total value of $2.5 billion. The new city aims for $50 billion in projects in its first phase, including green spaces and residential areas built to 'green construction standards'.

item.title: World Bank to provide over 420 million somoni to Tajikistan for agriculture and child development
item.description: The World Bank will allocate over 420 million Tajik somoni to Tajikistan to support the agriculture sector and child development initiatives. The majority of these funds will be provided as loans. Further details are available.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reports Arrest of 15 Customs and Border Service Employees
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov announced the detention of approximately 15 customs and border service employees on suspicion of smuggling. He stated that these officials were facilitating contraband and collecting bribes. Hidden camera footage reportedly shows systematic bribery. The announcement follows the dismissal of the heads of the customs and border services on October 9.
